doc.title: Pete Barbutti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 8, 2022

chapter: Vegas groups and Spokane solo years
title: Building a jazz group with Capitol deal, then collapse
summary: With Mike Wofford, Richie Matteson and Kay Brown he gets a Capitol deal, but the group walks out at Tahoe leaving him in debt; Frank Ross urges him to go solo.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Yeah. Anyway this guy Lee Dear said, “Look, why don’t you put together the group that you want and I’ll sign the contract, you can stay here.” So I got Mike Wofford on piano, who is an internationally known jazz player, a bass player from Lake Tahoe named Chuck DeLora who is a great player, Richie Matteson, who is like a great, great jazz educator. He was at North Texas State and then he went to North Florida and won every award there and we got a girl singer who was married to Maynard Ferguson years ago, a girl named Kay Brown. So we had three horns, three rhythm, and a girl singer. And Richie and I put our heads together and wrote — Richie especially was way above me man, he wrote unbelievable stuff. And we were together like three months and Capitol Records signed us to a recording deal the group was really strong. And then one night we were working at Lake Tahoe and our manager showed up and said, “I’m sorry about the problems.” “What problems?” He said, “Well this guy said this, and this guy.” And like overnight the group — everybody left. And I had signed for all the uniforms and the singer’s gowns and everything. So everybody took off and I was living in a rented house in Vegas with three kids and my wife was pregnant with the fourth. Had no income. So it was a real bad time. And then I went to see Frank Ross from the Mary Kay trio. They were like big stars in Vegas. I went to see Frank Ross and Frank said, “You’ve got to go on your own. You shouldn’t be with a group.” And he says, “I’m going to call an agent, he’s going to call you.” So this agent calls me and said, “I have a gig for you in Spokane, Washington.” I never heard of Spokane. I’d heard of Seattle but I’d never heard of Spokane. He said, “It’s some kind of steak house or something called The Stockyards Inn in Spokane and it doesn’t pay much but —” I said, “Okay but” I said, George Burke was the agent’s name — forgive me for remembering these names, this is like sixty years ago
